skill.name: image-edit
skill.description: Routes image-editing requests to four RunComfy models for batch edits, multilingual text replacement, precise local changes, and mask-based inpainting.
skill.summary: Choose a suitable RunComfy image model and generate a focused edit command.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, placeholder URLs, and ellipses misread as path traversal. The skill intentionally installs and invokes a third-party CLI, then sends prompts and image references to RunComfy. Its single-quoted JSON templates can permit shell injection if an agent interpolates untrusted text without robust escaping.

remediation.issue: User text can be interpolated into single-quoted shell JSON.
remediation.suggestion: Pass structured input through argv, stdin, or a generated JSON file. Never concatenate prompts or URLs into a shell command string.

remediation.issue: The setup installs and authenticates a third-party global CLI.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an exact CLI version and require explicit confirmation before installation, login, or the first remote edit command.

remediation.issue: Prompts and image references are processed by RunComfy servers.
remediation.suggestion: Require user consent, explain retention and billing terms, and warn against confidential assets or publicly exposed sensitive images.

semantic_findings.title: Potential Shell Injection Through Prompt Interpolation
semantic_findings.description: The examples place JSON inside single-quoted shell arguments, while user prompt text enters that JSON. An unescaped apostrophe could terminate the quote and inject shell syntax before the CLI receives the value.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The shell templates and user-input flow are explicit, but actual exploitability depends on how the agent constructs and escapes argv at runtime.

semantic_findings.title: Third-Party Processing of Prompts and Image References

content.user_title: Edit Images with Intent-Matched AI Models
content.value_statement: Choosing the wrong image model wastes time and reduces edit quality. This skill routes each request to a suitable RunComfy model with focused parameters.
actual_capabilities: Routes single or batch edits to Nano Banana Edit, with up to 20 input images and four outputs.
Uses GPT Image 2 Edit for multilingual text replacement, layout changes, and compositions with up to 10 references.
Uses Flux Kontext Pro for one-image, one-instruction local edits with preservation guidance.
Uses Z-Image Turbo Inpaint for mask-based removal or replacement with strength and control settings.
Builds RunComfy CLI requests and downloads generated images to a selected output directory.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and a valid login or API token.
Input images and masks must use publicly accessible HTTPS URLs for the documented routes.
Selects one model route per call and does not blend multiple model pipelines.
Quality, input counts, output sizes, latency, and availability depend on the selected model.

use_cases.title: Localize Campaign Artwork
use_cases.description: Replace headlines in multiple scripts while preserving photography, branding, layout, and visual identity.

use_cases.title: Standardize Product Galleries
use_cases.description: Apply consistent backgrounds, dimensions, and presentation across a batch of product images.

use_cases.title: Clean Masked Regions
use_cases.description: Remove distractions or replace selected regions while preserving nearby textures, edges, and lighting.

prompt_templates.title: Make a Basic Edit
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit [image URL]. Keep [elements] unchanged and change [target] to [desired result]. Save the result as [format].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one clear image change.

prompt_templates.title: Edit a Consistent Batch
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply [single edit] to [image URLs]. Preserve [identity or branding], lock [aspect ratio] and [resolution], and create [count] outputs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate batch editing with consistent dimensions.

prompt_templates.title: Compose References and Replace Text
prompt_templates.prompt: Use image 1 as primary and images 2-[n] as references. Replace [text] with [exact text] in [script], preserving [layout details].
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced multilingual composition using several references.

prompt_templates.title: Control a Masked Inpaint
prompt_templates.prompt: Inpaint [region] using [image URL] and [mask URL]. Preserve [surroundings], set strength [value], control scale [value], and seed [number].
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced region replacement with reproducible controls.

output_examples.input: A product team supplies 12 square SKU images and requests a consistent light gray studio background.
output_examples.output: Nano Banana Edit is selected. Twelve PNG images retain product identity, framing, and square dimensions with a consistent studio background.

output_examples.input: A designer requests a Japanese headline on an English poster while preserving the photograph and brand mark.
output_examples.output: GPT Image 2 Edit is selected. The headline changes to Japanese while the source layout, photograph, and branding remain stable.

output_examples.input: A retoucher provides a street photograph and mask covering overhead cables.
output_examples.output: Z-Image Turbo Inpaint is selected. The cables are removed while rooflines, sky color, and unmasked regions remain consistent.

best_practices: State preservation requirements before the requested change.
Use one clear edit per pass and name precise locations.
Lock aspect ratio, resolution, and seed when consistency or repeatability matters.
anti_patterns: Do not place secrets or confidential assets in publicly accessible image URLs.
Do not combine unrelated edits in one prompt.
Do not interpolate untrusted prompts directly into shell command strings.

faq.question: How does the skill choose a model?
faq.answer: It maps the requested edit type to one of four documented RunComfy model routes.

faq.question: Is a RunComfy account required?
faq.answer: Yes. The CLI requires an authenticated account or a valid RUNCOMFY_TOKEN value.

faq.question: Can it edit image batches?
faq.answer: Yes. Nano Banana Edit accepts up to 20 input images and can produce up to four outputs.

faq.question: Can it replace non-Latin text?
faq.answer: Yes. The GPT Image 2 route targets multilingual text replacement and layout preservation.

faq.question: When is a mask required?
faq.answer: Z-Image Turbo Inpaint requires a grayscale mask where white marks edits and black marks preserved areas.

faq.question: Are images processed locally?
faq.answer: No. RunComfy servers process prompts and image references, while the CLI downloads completed outputs locally.
